title: No AI Slop packages a plain-language editing pass as an agent skill
friendlyTitle: A writing skill that removes common AI-sounding phrases
summary: No AI Slop is an MIT-licensed editing skill that checks for more than 20 recurring patterns in generic AI prose, including canned contrasts, throat-clearing, vague attribution, and inflated conclusions. It can revise text while listing its changes or only flag matching passages.
friendlySummary: This open skill looks for repeated patterns that make AI writing sound generic. It can edit the text or simply show where those patterns appear.
whyItMatters: Writers can add it to supported assistants as a final editing pass without asking the model to rewrite everything into a new voice. Its explicit checklist is also easy to inspect, adapt, or use manually when polishing AI-assisted drafts.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use it as a final check to make AI-assisted writing clearer while keeping your own voice.
